citations.claim: Nvidia reported Q1 fiscal 2025 revenue of $26 billion, up 18% sequentially and 262% year over year, above its $24 billion outlook.
citations.source_text: Revenue of 26 billion was up 18% sequentially and up 262% year on year and well above our outlook of 24 billion.

citations.claim: GAAP gross margin rose sequentially to 78.4%, and non-GAAP gross margin to 78.9%, with lower inventory charges.
citations.source_text: Okay, moving to the rest of the P&L, gap growth margin expanded sequentially to 78.4% and non-gap growth margins to 78.9% on lower inventory charges.

citations.claim: Automotive revenue was $329 million, up 17% sequentially and 11% year‑over‑year.
citations.source_text: Moving to automotive, revenue was 329 million, up 17% sequentially and up 11% year on year.

citations.claim: GAAP operating expenses rose 10% sequentially and non-GAAP operating expenses rose 13%, mainly reflecting higher compensation costs and compute and infrastructure investments.
citations.source_text: sequentially, gap operating expenses were up 10% and non-gap operating expenses were up 13%, primarily reflecting higher compensation-related costs and increased compute and infrastructure investments.

citations.claim: Gaming revenue was $2.65 billion, down 8% sequentially and up 18% year over year, consistent with Nvidia’s earlier outlook for a seasonal decline.
citations.source_text: Moving to gaming and AI PCs, gaming revenue of $2.65 billion was down 8% sequentially and up 18% year-on-year consistent with our outlook for a seasonal decline.

citations.claim: Nvidia said its China Data Center revenue was significantly below the level before new export-control restrictions in October.
citations.source_text: Our data center revenue in China is down significantly from the level prior to the imposition of the new export control restrictions in October.
